subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint — GPU mix, regional throughput & next steps for Nimbus Analytics
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@nimbus.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP checkpoint — initial sizing ask and throughput targets

Hi Helen / Nimbus team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our MAP we said we'd align on a recommended GPU mix and regional capacity targets so your evaluation can exercise the worst-case latency and throughput scenarios. Attached is a working workbook (nimbus-map-v4.xlsx) with three scenarios: baseline eval, production pilot, and sustained commit.

Quick notes:
- Baseline eval: 2 r3.8x GPUs (A100 equivalent) in us-west for 8k-context tests, target ~25 qps peak with conservative batching.
- Production pilot: 4 r4.16x (L40-like) split us-west / us-east, target 50 qps peak and 150k tokens/min sustained.
- Sustained commit: 8 r4.32x across us-west/us-east + fallbacks in us-central, goal 120 qps and KV-cache prewarm for common prefixes.

Can you confirm which scenario you want us to size for next week's pilot? Also calling out a few open items for the MAP:
1) Finalize target SLOs per API route (ingest vs. generate). Owner: Nimbus (Helen).
2) Decide acceptable fallback policy (downscale vs model-variant). Owner: Nimbus + Redwood (Marissa).
3) Confirm procurement timeline for reserved nodes. Owner: Nimbus Procurement.

I'll ask Marissa and Karthik to include recommended batching/quantization knobs that preserve quality for your prompt set.

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: nimbus-map-v4.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Helen Park <helen.park@nimbus.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — initial sizing ask and throughput targets

Diego / team,

Appreciate the workbook — useful framing. A few quick replies from our side: we want to run the production pilot (4-node target) but we need the pilot to demonstrate both latency under 250ms 95th for short-form queries and a sustained throughput test at 40 qps for 30 minutes. Procurement is willing to fast-track a short-term reserved window for that pilot week.

Open clarifications:
- Region: prefer us-west primary with us-east as warm-failover.
- GPU mix: if L40-class is strongly preferred for your runtime, call that out; if A100-equivalent suffices at lower cost we can evaluate that trade-off.
- Security: we need a short SOC2 evidence bundle for the pilot.

We'll confirm SLOs by EOD Thu.

Thanks,

Helen Park
Head of Platform, Nimbus Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helen Park <helen.park@nimbus.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — initial sizing ask and throughput targets

Adding our recommended knobs after running Nimbus prompt set on smaller-scale tests (see gpu-sku-comparison.pdf):

Summary recommendations (pilot / production):
- Pilot (4 nodes): prefer mixed pool: 2 x L40-class (r4.16x) + 2 x A100-equivalent (r3.8x) as a cost/latency compromise. This gives consistent sub-250ms 95th for short responses while letting some heavier long-context samples route to L40s.
- Batching: dynamic batching with max batch 16 for generate endpoints, Batching latency floor 15ms.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for the top 20 prompt templates; expected hit rate 35-45% reducing tokens/min by ~20%.
- Quantization: per-model calibration with 4-bit weight reduction on A100-equivalent nodes; keep L40s in full precision for tail quality.

Throughput projections (pilot):
- Peak qps: 45 qps (sustained test target 40 qps for 30m)
- Tokens/min: 135k
- Expected container footprint: 4 nodes x 128GB GPU RAM equivalent

Action items from our side:
- Provide tuned runbook for pilot (Marissa) — delivers Monday EOD.
- Provide SOC2 evidence snapshot for pilot (Laura) — deliver Fri EOD.
- Update MAP doc with failover policy (Diego + Marissa) — in progress.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: gpu-sku-comparison.pdf (report)]
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@nimbus.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — initial sizing ask and throughput targets (checkpoint & next steps)

Helen — thanks for the clarity. Quick checkpoint following Marissa's tests and our internal alignment. Below is a concise MAP checkpoint update and ownership summary ahead of the pilot run week (target week of 2026-07-05).

MAP checkpoint — 2026-06-20
- Selected pilot configuration: mixed pool (2 x L40-class, 2 x A100-equivalent) in us-west primary, us-east warm-failover. Rationale: preserves tail-quality while controlling cost.
- Pilot throughput target: 40 qps sustained for 30 min; 95th latency target <250ms for short queries.
- Token throughput target: ~135k tokens/min for pilot load profile.
- Fallback policy: automatic region failover to us-east with model-variant downgrade to A100-equivalent only if cluster capacity degraded >20% for >60s. (Marissa to draft exact thresholds.)

Action items and owners:
- Marissa Cole: Pilot runbook + batching/quantization parameters (deliverable: runbook PDF). Due: 2026-06-22
- Laura Bennett: SOC2 evidence snapshot and short compliance checklist for pilot. Due: 2026-06-19 (in flight) — Laura to confirm delivery timestamp.
- Nimbus (Helen): Confirm SLO sign-off and procurement window for reserved nodes. Due: 2026-06-24
- Diego Fernandez: Update MAP doc and provide orchestration template + fallback policy draft. Due: 2026-06-23
- Karthik Iyer: Final throughput test harness and load script for the 30-min sustained run. Due: 2026-06-28

Attachments referenced: nimbus-map-v4.xlsx (scenario workbook), gpu-sku-comparison.pdf (internal SKU report), regional-throughput-projections.csv (load profiles).

Next check-in: Wed 2026-06-23 10:00 PDT — 30m sync to confirm Laura's SOC2 snapshot and Nimbus procurement window. Calendar invite to follow.

Regards,

Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: regional-throughput-projections.csv (csv)]
